cards.front: Recall a key point about Stellar Evolution & Nucleosynthesis
cards.back: Nucleosynthesis is the process by which stars create heavier elements from lighter ones through nuclear fusion

cards.front: Recall a key point about Stellar Evolution & Nucleosynthesis
cards.back: Main-sequence stars fuse hydrogen to helium via the proton-proton chain (lower mass) or CNO cycle (higher mass)

cards.front: Recall a key point about Stellar Evolution & Nucleosynthesis
cards.back: The triple-alpha process fuses three helium nuclei into carbon in red giant cores

cards.front: Recall a key point about Stellar Evolution & Nucleosynthesis
cards.back: Massive stars can fuse elements up to iron (Fe) in successive shell layers — iron is the endpoint as fusion beyond iron absorbs energy

cards.front: Recall a key point about Stellar Evolution & Nucleosynthesis
cards.back: Elements heavier than iron are created during supernovae (r-process) and neutron star mergers

cards.front: Recall a key point about Stellar Evolution & Nucleosynthesis
cards.back: We are made of stellar material — most elements in our bodies were forged in stars

cards.front: What should you know about gcse astronomy exam tips — stellar evolution & nucleosynthesis?
cards.back: 1. For Stellar Evolution & Nucleosynthesis questions, define key terms before explaining processes 2. Use 'because' to link cause and effect in your explanations 3. Include units in all calculations and show your working for method marks 4. When evaluating Stellar Evolution & Nucleosynthesis, consider both the quality of evidence and practical implications 5. For extended response questions, plan your answer: identify AO1/AO2/AO3 requirements first
